items.titleEn: UBS picks 3 luxury stocks with up to 25% upside for 2027
items.summaryEn: Buy Richemont. UBS expects 10% organic sales growth in 2027 and jewellery-led outperformance (jewellery +19% at constant currency). The stock sold off on “normalisation” fears, but UBS also points to strong margin delivery and Richemont’s net cash (€7.7B) to absorb raw-material pressure. This sets up a rebound as investors refocus on jewellery strength and earnings durability into 2027. Key Risk: Jewellery growth keeps slowing faster than expected and margins compress, forcing UBS-style upside targets to reset lower. Buy Ferrari. UBS’s bull case is pricing power: operating profit rose even as shipments slipped (profit +12% with only -1% vehicles). Industrial free cash flow jumped 43%, and the order book visibility into 2028 plus higher-value model mix (F80/personalisation) should keep earnings growing even if luxury car demand softens.

items.titleEn: Free SpaceX stock: what's the catch in Elon Musk's $18 billion giveaway?
items.summaryEn: Buy SpaceX Class A common. The giveaway is a forced, long-duration retail shareholder creation: shares must be held inside Trump Accounts for years, so selling pressure is structurally delayed. That supports a higher floor for the stock into the restriction window, even if near-term headlines create volatility. Musk’s personal match later (June 2027) adds another wave of incremental demand as the program scales. Key Risk: SpaceX fundamentals break—e.g., a major launch/contract setback or a deal that materially dilutes value (like a Tesla all-stock combination) and drives the stock down despite the lock-up. Sell SpaceX Class A common if you can short or use puts. The corporate donation requires issuing new Class A shares tied to “active Trump Accounts,” which is dilution with uncertain magnitude because “active” is not precisely defined. If the number of qualifying accounts is higher than expected, dilution could outweigh the demand created by the lock-up, especially if markets price in a Tesla/merger overhang.

items.titleEn: Nvidia stock: could S&P's downgrade threat trigger another crash?
items.summaryEn: Buy iShares iBoxx $Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF (LQD) selectively vs. high-yield AI credit exposure; avoid new risk in AI infrastructure lenders. The article flags hyperscaler “circular financing” worries and extreme stress in AI-related debt (e.g., CoreWeave 2031 yields near 18%). If lenders get selective, data-center expansion slows, pressuring AI capex and ultimately NVDA demand—so position for credit to tighten rather than chase AI equity momentum. Key Risk: AI credit spreads mean-revert fast (hyperscalers refinance smoothly), and AI infrastructure funding stays abundant, lifting risk assets including AI-linked equities. Sell NASDAQ:NVDA. S&P put AA issuer and senior unsecured debt on CreditWatch Negative; CDS hit a record (147 bps) and the market is already pricing governance/export-control uncertainty. Even if the cut is only one notch, the stock can re-rate lower because investors will demand a higher risk premium while the board proves oversight. Key catalyst: any further negative headlines before/around Huang’s Dec 3 Senate testimony.

items.titleEn: Why Samsung and SK Hynix stock rebound could be a classic bull trap
items.summaryEn: Buy Samsung Electronics. It’s the cleaner way to own Korea memory exposure while the market is panicking: foreign selling is reversible (foreigners already turned net buyers Thursday), and Samsung’s broader earnings base can cushion a memory slowdown better than pure-play peers. If Micron’s downgrade is “the bad news,” the next move is stabilization and mean reversion in the stock after the sharp sell-off. Key risk: memory pricing falls faster than expected and drags Samsung’s consolidated earnings materially, not just segment margins. Key Risk: Memory prices drop faster than expected and hit Samsung’s consolidated earnings. Sell SK Hynix. The rebound looks like a bull trap: Micron was downgraded on oversupply risk and BNP pushed DRAM/NAND balance earlier (mid-2027), which typically hits pricing first. SK Hynix is already warning on inventory adjustments in 2Q/3Q 2027, so rallies are likely to fade as the market reprices earnings down. Key risk: a sustained AI-driven pricing upcycle that keeps DRAM/NAND ASPs rising year-over-year through 2027, overriding oversupply fears.

items.titleEn: Gold, silver reverse early losses as Wall Street rebounds ahead of Thanksgiving - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were higher in late U.S. trading Wednesday, staging a recovery from steep morning losses as falling Treasury yields and a broad rebound in North American equities helped stabilize precious metals despite stronger-than-expected U.S. economic growth and persistent inflation. Gold recovered above $3,570.00 an ounce after briefly falling below $3,450.00, while silver rebounded above $41 after earlier testing its lowest levels in more than a year. The recovery coincided with a sharp reversal on Wall Street, where major indexes erased much of their early losses as technology-sector selling moderated ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. Spot gold was trading near $3,576.30 an ounce, up $21.20, or 0.60%, while silver was trading near $41.120, up $0.320 or 0.78% on the session. Gold traded between $3,426.40 and $3,590.00 during the session, while silver's range extended from $38.090 to $41.590. Wednesday's U.S. economic data highlighted the resilience of the American economy despite persistent inflation and concerns about slowing activity in selected sectors. The October personal consumption expenditures price index increased 0.3% on the month and 3.8% from a year earlier, compared with September's annual increase of 3.7%. The core PCE index, excluding food and energy, also increased 0.3% on the month, while annual core inflation accelerated to 3.3% , reinforcing concerns about underlying price pressures. Meanwhile, the second estimate of third-quarter gross domestic product indicated that the economy expanded at an annualized 4.3%, exceeding expectations near 3.6%. Personal income increased 0.7% in October, while consumer spending advanced 0.3%, although inflation-adjusted spending was essentially unchanged. Durable goods orders rose just 0.2%, indicating a more uneven picture of business investment. The combination of strong economic growth, persistent inflation and slower real consumer spending highlighted the increasingly difficult policy environment facing the Federal Reserve as it considers further monetary tightening.

items.titleEn: Plug Power stock jumped as US indices plunged: Will the gains hold?
items.summaryEn: Buy Plug Power (PLUG) for a squeeze-and-reversion move after the 14% jump. The article shows improving fundamentals (revenue +13%, gross margin improving to -3%, equipment sales $105M, GenDrive deployments 1,136) plus a likely oversold-to-stabilizing setup (RSI not deeply oversold, still below trend indicators). Target $1.25, then reassess for continuation. Key Risk: Another ATM/dilution raise that overwhelms the improved quarter and forces the stock back below $0.80. Sell Plug Power (PLUG) short on rallies if it fails to hold the post-news bounce. The stock is still below all moving averages and the article flags ongoing dilution risk; short interest (~20%) can fuel volatility both ways, but it also means any disappointment can cascade. Use a tight thesis window: if price can’t sustain above the recent spike area, expect a return to the downtrend toward $0.80.

items.titleEn: Why is HP stock one of the top performing stocks in today's session?
items.summaryEn: Buy HP Inc. (HPQ). The stock is ripping on better-than-expected fiscal 2027 earnings guidance, and the company explicitly targets Personal Systems operating margins rising from ~3% toward 5–7% through fiscal 2027. Even if the quarter’s beat had “low-quality” tariff-refund help, the forward margin path plus premium/AI-enabled PC mix is a real catalyst for multiple expansion if PC demand stabilizes. Key Risk: Tariff refunds and accounting noise prove to be the main driver, and margins fail to climb toward 5–7% because PC demand keeps sliding and component costs stay elevated. Sell Dell Technologies (DELL) versus HPQ. Dell also beat earnings and guided better, yet the market punished it (-5% on the day) while HP rallied. That divergence suggests investors are more willing to believe HP’s margin-recovery story than Dell’s, so the relative trade is to fade DELL until it shows the same credible margin trajectory.

items.titleEn: Top 4 reasons the S&P 500 Index and ETFs like VOO, SPY, IVV are set to rebound
items.summaryEn: Fear & Greed at 15 (extreme fear) plus forward P/E ~16 (lowest in years) sets up a classic “panic selling” rebound. Earnings growth is still strong (~32.9% vs ~29% expected), so the selloff looks more sentiment-driven than fundamentals-driven. Technicals: hold of ~6,900 and a likely move toward ~7,500 supports a near-term bounce. Buy SPY for broad exposure to the rebound. Key Risk: Rates rise again faster than expected, forcing a fresh de-rating of the whole market. The article flags NVDA forward P/E ~16 vs a 5-year average ~40, while the company is actively repurchasing ($150B+) and just delivered strong earnings. If “AI bubble fears” fade, NVDA should rebound harder than the index because it’s the highest-quality AI bellwether and the valuation gap is already priced in. Buy NVDA shares (or NVDA call options for leverage).
